mainTopic: The end of the ditches discussion and the close of פרק בית כור. Then the opening of פרק יש נוחלין: its משנה on four inheritance groups and the גמרא's question about the order of the משנה's list.
overview: First, the גמרא finishes a discussion from the previous page about two ditches dug to keep wild animals from jumping in: a larger חריץ and a smaller בן חריץ. It asks why both are needed. A wide ditch alone lets the animal stand inside it and jump. A narrow ditch alone lets the animal stand on its edge and jump. So both are dug, one טפח apart. Then a הדרן closes פרק בית כור, and a new chapter, פרק יש נוחלין, begins. Its משנה sorts relatives into four groups: those who inherit both ways, those who only receive, those who only pass on, and those who do neither. The גמרא then asks why the משנה lists the father inheriting from his sons before the sons inheriting from the father. It gives a first reason the sons should come first: we do not open with misfortune. The rest of the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ditches stop animals from jumping in
steps.stepSummary: The line from the previous page finishes: the ditches are there so a wild animal cannot jump in.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that a wild animal will not jump.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence from the previous page, giving the reason for the ditches: they keep wild animals from jumping in. This sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ditches are dug, a larger חריץ and a smaller בן חריץ. Their job is to stop an animal from leaping over the boundary and doing damage. Once we know the goal, the גמרא can ask whether both ditches are really needed.

phrases.english: so that a wild animal will not jump.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page, about why the two ditches are dug.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The purpose of the חריץ and בן חריץ is to stop wild animals from jumping in.

steps.title: Why not dig only the big ditch?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the smaller ditch is needed. Why not dig just the large one?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him make a large ditch and not make a small ditch!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for two ditches: if the goal is to stop animals, one big ditch should be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes a single large ditch already blocks the animal. If so, the smaller בן חריץ looks like extra work for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'son of a ditch': the smaller ditch

phrases.english: But let him make a (large) ditch
and not make a small ditch!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַעֲבֵיד חָרִיץ וְלָא לַעֲבֵיד בֶּן חָרִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for both ditches named in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the smaller ditch (בן חריץ).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the large ditch alone blocks animals, the small one is unnecessary.

steps.title: A wide ditch lets the animal stand inside and jump
steps.stepSummary: A big ditch alone fails, because the animal can stand inside it and jump out from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is wide, the animal stands inside it and jumps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a wide ditch alone does not work, because the animal can climb down into it and leap from inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wide ditch has room for the animal to stand in. From there it can still jump across. So the big ditch alone does not do the job.

phrases.english: Since it is wide,
the animal stands inside it and jumps.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: a single large ditch does not fully work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One big ditch is enough to stop animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wide ditch gives the animal a place to stand and jump, so it is not enough alone.

steps.title: Then why not dig only the small ditch?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around: maybe the small ditch alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him make a small ditch and not make a large ditch!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: if a wide ditch is a problem, why not dig only the narrow one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed the wide ditch was the weak point. So the obvious next idea is to drop it and keep only the narrow בן חריץ.

phrases.english: Then let him make a small ditch
and not make a large ditch!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַעֲבֵיד בֶּן חָרִיץ וְלָא לַעֲבֵיד חָרִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 3's answer to ask the reverse question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the larger ditch (חריץ).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wide ditch is the problem, use only the narrow one.

steps.title: A narrow ditch lets the animal stand on its edge and jump
steps.stepSummary: A small ditch alone also fails, because the animal can stand on its edge and jump across.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is small, the animal stands on its edge and jumps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a narrow ditch alone fails too, because the animal can just stand at its edge and leap over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A narrow ditch is easy to jump. Each ditch alone has a weakness, so together they block the animal.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ditches are needed. A wide ditch alone lets the animal stand inside it, and a narrow ditch alone lets the animal jump over it from the edge.

phrases.english: Since it is small,
the animal stands on its edge and jumps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4, which completes the case for needing both ditches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: a single small ditch does not fully work.
steps.terutzMaskana: A narrow ditch is easy to jump from its edge, so both ditches are required.

steps.title: How far apart are the two ditches?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much space separates the large ditch from the small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is there between the large ditch and the small ditch?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a measurement question about the distance between the two ditches. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know both ditches are needed, we need the exact layout. This question asks for the gap between them.

phrases.english: And how much is there between the large ditch and the small ditch?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why both ditches exist to how they are laid out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distance between the חריץ and the בן חריץ.

steps.title: One handbreadth apart
steps.stepSummary: The gap between the two ditches is one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is one טפח, so the ditches are dug one handbreadth apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a fixed size for the gap between the ditches. With it, the discussion of the ditches and the whole chapter comes to an end.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a standard small measure

phrases.english: A handbreadth.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ditches are one טפח apart.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק בית כור
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for the chapter called בית כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, בית כור.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the traditional line said when finishing a chapter. It closes פרק בית כור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן does not teach a law. It marks the end of this chapter, which dealt with selling fields. A new subject, inheritance, starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula for finishing a chapter
Name of the chapter just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, Beit Kor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: Four kinds of inheritance relationships
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה opens by saying relatives fall into four groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who inherit and pass on an inheritance; there are those who inherit but do not pass on; those who pass on but do not inherit; and those who neither inherit nor pass on.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה of פרק יש נוחלין opens with a list of four headings for how relatives inherit from each other. The details come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two directions to keep track of. 'נוחלין' means the person receives an inheritance from the relative, and 'מנחילין' means the relative receives from him. Some pairs go both ways, some only one way, and some not at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They inherit, meaning they receive from the relative
They bequeath, meaning the relative receives from them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up נוחלין (I receive from you) and מנחילין (you receive from me). Every pair in the משנה is about which direction the inheritance flows.

phrases.english: There are those who inherit and bequeath,
and there are those who inherit but do not bequeath;
those who bequeath but do not inherit;
and those who neither inherit nor bequeath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives fall into four groups depending on which direction inheritance flows between them.

steps.title: Relatives who inherit both ways
steps.stepSummary: A father and sons, and paternal brothers, inherit from each other in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: These inherit and bequeath: a father from sons, sons from a father, and brothers from the same father. They inherit and bequeath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the first group: relatives who inherit from each other both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Father and son each inherit from the other, depending on who dies first. Brothers who share a father also inherit from each other in both directions.

phrases.english: And these inherit and bequeath:
a father with regard to his sons,
and sons with regard to their father,
and brothers from the same father,
they inherit and bequeath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first group from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father and sons, and paternal brothers, inherit from each other both ways.

steps.title: Relatives who inherit but do not pass on
steps.stepSummary: A man inherits from his mother and from his wife, and sisters' sons inherit, but not the other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man from his mother, a man from his wife, and sons of sisters: they inherit but do not bequeath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the second group: relatives who receive an inheritance but do not pass one back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son inherits his mother, but she does not inherit him. A husband inherits his wife, but she does not inherit him. Sons of sisters inherit from their mother's brothers, but those uncles do not inherit from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Sons of sisters, nephews through a sister

phrases.english: A man with regard to his mother,
and a man with regard to his wife,
and sons of sisters,
inherit but do not bequeath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second group from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man from his mother, a husband from his wife, and sisters' sons inherit one way only.

steps.title: Relatives who pass on but do not inherit
steps.stepSummary: A woman to her sons, a wife to her husband, and maternal uncles: they pass on but do not inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman to her sons, a woman to her husband, and brothers of the mother: they bequeath but do not inherit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the third group. These are the same pairs as the last step, seen from the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 11. The mother, the wife, and the mother's brothers are the ones whose property goes to the son, husband, or nephew, but they get nothing back.

phrases.english: A woman with regard to her sons,
and a woman with regard to her husband,
and brothers of the mother,
bequeath but do not inherit.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mother, a wife, and maternal uncles pass on an inheritance but do not receive one from these relatives.

steps.title: Maternal brothers: neither way
steps.stepSummary: Brothers who share only a mother do not inherit from each other at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And brothers from the same mother neither inherit nor bequeath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the fourth group: brothers through the mother only, who have no inheritance link at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare step 10: brothers from the same father inherit from each other both ways. Brothers who share only a mother do not, so in inheritance the father's side is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers from the same mother only

steps.whatToRemember: The four groups: both ways (father and sons, paternal brothers); receive only (son from mother, husband from wife, sisters' sons); give only (mother, wife, maternal uncles); neither (maternal brothers).
steps.whyThisMatters: Putting paternal brothers (both ways) next to maternal brothers (neither way) shows that inheritance follows the father's family. That idea runs through this whole chapter.

phrases.english: And brothers from the same mother
neither inherit nor bequeath.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאַחִין מִן הָאֵם לֹא נוֹחֲלִין וְלֹא מַנְחִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the fourth group from step 9 and contrasts with paternal brothers in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Maternal half-brothers have no inheritance relationship with each other.

steps.title: Why does the משנה list the father inheriting from his sons first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה opens with 'the father from the sons' instead of 'the sons from the father'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה teach 'the father from the sons' first? It should teach 'the sons from the father' first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking about the order of its words. It asks why the משנה starts with the father inheriting from his sons instead of the sons inheriting from the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the משנה said fathers and sons inherit from each other, and it named the father first. The גמרא pushes back: the normal case is sons inheriting from their father, so that case should come first.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה
Why is it different? What is the reason for this?
Let it teach (it should have said)

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is the reason that it teaches
'the father from the sons' first?
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words from step 10: the father inherits from his sons.

phrases.english: Let it teach 'the sons from the father' first

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in steps 9-13, focusing on the order of the list in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the משנה, which puts 'the father from the sons' before 'the sons from the father'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sons inheriting from their father is the normal case, so it seems it should be listed first.

steps.title: First reason: we do not open with something sad
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its question: one reason the sons should come first is that we do not open with misfortune.
steps.simpleTranslation: One reason: we do not begin with misfortune.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first reason to support its question. We do not like to open with something sad, so the משנה should not open with the father inheriting from his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father inheriting from his sons is a sad case, because it means the sons died. Opening with that seems wrong, which makes the question stronger. The word חדא ('one') tells us this is only the first reason. The real answer to the question has not come yet.

keyTerms.meaning: One (the first of a few reasons)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the answer. It is a reason that makes the question stronger. The גמרא is still asking why the משנה put the father first.

phrases.english: One reason: with beginning with misfortune
phrases.notes: 'One' means this is the first reason. The father inheriting from his sons is the sad case, since the sons have died.

phrases.english: we do not begin;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the first supporting reason to the question raised in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: Opening the משנה with 'the father from the sons'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case points to the sons having died, and we avoid opening with misfortune. So the משנה should have opened with the sons inheriting from the father.
